title: paged KV cache: block manager pinning and allocator reuse optimizations
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Improve paged KV cache stability and memory usage by reusing block allocator arenas and adding block pinning semantics.
Latency: ~8-12% p99 improvement on long-context workloads in our internal benchmark.
Throughput: ~10-15% higher sustained throughput for generation-heavy workloads due to reduced lock contention and allocator churn.
description: Context: the paged KV cache block manager has seen increased allocation churn and fragmentation under long-context continuous-batching workloads. Frequent allocate/free cycles for small blocks and conservative eviction policies cause extra CPU work and transient memory pressure that impacts tail latency and throughput. Motivation: reduce allocator churn, avoid unnecessary evictions of hot KV blocks, and reduce lock contention in the hot path. Summary: this PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) a block allocator reuse pool with per-device arenas to avoid repeated mmap/munmap and allocator metadata churn; and 2) block pin/unpin semantics in the block manager so frequently-accessed blocks (hot prefixes / KV cache hits) can be temporarily pinned to prevent eviction during scheduling/dispatch. Together these changes reduce CPU allocator overhead, reduce fragmentation, and lower eviction-induced cache misses. Detailed changes (high level): - allocator.rs: add ReusePool and per-device Arena wrappers. Pools are sized heuristically based on recent allocation histogram and reclaimed under memory pressure. Allocator now exposes try_reuse()/release_reuse() APIs used by the block manager. - block_manager.rs: add pin_block/unpin_block APIs and integrate with eviction LRU. Pinned blocks are skipped by background eviction and by aggressive preemption heuristics; pinnedness is reference-counted and thread-safe. - kv_cache_integration.rs: use allocator reuse for ephemeral allocations during continuous batching and for KV block materialization paths. Reduce the use of global locks in the hot path (migrate a portion to per-shard mutexes and atomic ops). - tests/: unit tests for pin/unpin races, allocator reuse lifecycle, and a synthetic benchmark that emulates long-context continuous batching. - bench/serving/: updated microbench harness to measure p50/p95/p99 improvements and memory footprint across different sequence-length distributions. Performance: internal bench runs (batching-heavy, seq_len=4096, steady-state) showed ~8% p99 reduction and ~12% throughput increase on a 16-GPU dedicated pool. Memory footprint reduced by ~20% under synthetic fragmentation workloads. Individual numbers vary by model and workload. Safety and compatibility: default behavior preserves the previous eviction policy - pinning is opt-in via a new config flag (kv.block_manager.enable_pinning) which defaults to true in canary builds. Allocator reuse is guarded behind kv.allocator.reuse_enabled and can be toggled at runtime. No public API surface changes for clients; internal API added for runtime components. Rollout plan: merge to main -> canary rollout to dedicated region us-west-2 with 2% traffic -> monitor p99, memory, and bench regressions -> increase to 20% if stable -> full rollout. Fallback: config flags allow disabling pinning or reuse quickly; block manager will gracefully fall back to previous allocate/free path. Testing: unit + integration + bench coverage included. Added targeted tests for concurrency (pin/unpin races) and a stress test that runs the allocator under heavy allocate/free churn. CI: full test suite + bench-lab smoke run. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: linked in Linear ENG-7241 - [x] Unit tests for pin/unpin and allocator reuse - [x] Integration tests for KV cache correctness under pinning - [x] Benchmarks & perf numbers included - [x] Config toggles for safe rollback - [x] Observability: added metrics for "kv.pinned_blocks", "kv.allocator_reuses", and eviction skips due to pinning Notes: kept the change scoped to block manager and allocator. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-7310 to expand pinning heuristics (frequency-based pinning) and to expose a top-k hot-block cache for prioritized pinning.

Marco Hernandez: The reuse pool growth heuristic looks conservative; suggest capping per-device pool size to avoid OOM in multi-tenant scenarios.
